To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a team approach, integrated support and differentiated learning activities and assessments can be effective in challenging and supporting students in IWLP classes.

a) a small number of international students who were enrolled in Beginners French – CEFR A1 – faced particular challenges in relation with their peers; b) a team teaching approach was developed to address the needs of these students; c) the module was redesigned to include integrated support and differentiated assessments; d) student feedback was positive and students made suggestions for further curriculum enhancements; e) a number of students who might have otherwise dropped out or been discouraged were able to complete and pass the module; f

the team teaching of Beginners French at the University of reading has been successful and that it has led to the development of a module which is challenging, supportive and empowering for all students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a pedagogically sound and effective response to the needs of international students and to the challenges of internationalisation.
how to make IWLP modules accessible to all students and how to ensure that they are challenging, supportive, and empowering.
the question of how a language programme can be designed to meet the needs of a range of learners, including students with different language levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the team teaching approach was successful and that the module was a success.
this module has provided a model for other IWLP modules in the university.
this module is successful in challenging, supporting and empowering international students in IWLP classes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the team’s efforts to support students in a challenging and empowering way resulted in a module that was well received by students.

a small change to the curriculum and assessment, in conjunction with student-centred learning, can have significant impact on students’ motivation, engagement, learning, achievement, and satisfaction with the language module.
we have been able to create a learning environment which is inclusive and which supports all students, whatever their background and level of proficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small team of committed teachers can respond creatively to the challenge of teaching and assessing students from diverse backgrounds and levels of proficiency.
a team of teachers can work together to support students with different needs and backgrounds, and at the same enhance the learning experience of the whole group.

the development of a supportive, challenging and empowering learning environment is possible even within the constraints of the CEFR and the UK Quality Assurance Agency’s Framework for Higher Education Qualifications.
